It solves the problem where camera poses are scaled by an arbitrary factor $s_i$, preventing the inference of metric depth from a single view [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that camera poses are scaled by an arbitrary factor $s_i$ which is different for each scene. It further explains that the proposed epipolar encoder resolves this scale ambiguity by associating cross-view pixel correspondences with positionally encoded depth values, allowing the inference of the per-scene scale factor $s_i$. This directly supports the claim that the method solves the problem of arbitrary scaling preventing metric depth inference from a single view (by using multi-view correspondence to resolve the scale).

A multi-view encoder component that resolves scale ambiguity by finding cross-view pixel correspondences and associating them with positionally encoded depth values, allowing the inference of the per-scene scale factor $s_i$ [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that the proposed 'multi-view encoder' (specifically an epipolar transformer) resolves scale ambiguity by finding 'cross-view pixel correspondences' (via epipolar attention) and associating them with 'positionally encoded depth values' (augmenting samples with positional encoding of triangulated depths). It further explains that this process allows the encoder to record correct depths consistent with the scene's arbitrary scale factor $s_i$, which is then used for depth prediction and Gaussian parameter prediction.
supported
